A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LightThinker research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material that was relocated or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results for two model families across four datasets, efficiency measurements, component and cache-size ablations, and a failure case.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds an equal-memory-budget inference-time comparison in Table 2.

M1.justification: The segmentation strategies, cache and output tokens, attention masks, training objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix B elaborates the existing compression operation rather than introducing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use Bespoke-Stratos-17k for training and GSM8K, MMLU, GPQA, and BBH for evaluation, alongside the retained long-generation efficiency test. The new memory-budget comparison uses existing tasks and datasets.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain CoT, Distill-R1, Vanilla, H2O, SepLLM, and AnLLM. The new timing experiment compares against the existing Vanilla baseline. System-1.5 and SoftThinking appear in a qualitative discussion table, without reported experimental evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds an equal-memory-budget timing protocol for Qwen, exploiting larger batches for LightThinker, alongside the retained equal-batch-size comparison. Existing training settings, prompts, greedy decoding, and output-length limits remain unchanged. The new experiment's numerical memory budget and batch sizes are unspecified.

E4.justification: v2 adds an analysis of throughput under equal memory constraints and reports qualitative inspection finding more repeated content with smaller caches in Appendix E.3. The existing component ablations, cache-size curves, compression distributions, and GSM8K failure case are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions show the same 95% confidence intervals for compression ratios in v1 Figure 5(d) and v2 Figure 4(d). No additional run counts, seeds, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises baseline accuracies: Qwen CoT GSM8K changes from 27.75 to 86.12; Qwen Distill-R1 MMLU/GPQA from 28.24/10.10 to 51.70/24.75; and Llama Distill-R1 MMLU/BBH from 22.01/37.58 to 53.46/61.21. LightThinker's original scores remain unchanged. New Table 2 reports mean times of 13.68 hours for Vanilla and 5.50 for LightThinker under equal memory, a newly reported setting rather than a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: New Appendix B gives a formal layer-level definition of the previously schematic compression operator, specifying segmented query/key/value matrices, masked attention weights, dimensions, and the weighted-value representation. The training objective and Dependency derivations remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: dynamic thought compression, the Dependency metric, and an efficiency–accuracy tradeoff demonstrated on four datasets and two model families. The headline Qwen efficiency claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The Limitations section contracts from nine points to three, dropping dedicated qualifications about Llama degradation, memory peaks, parameter-efficient tuning, data/model scaling, and reinforcement-learning compatibility. Section 4.2 changes the explanation for Distill-R1 underperformance from greedy-decoding repetition to instruction-following and answer-extraction difficulties. Appendix E adds explanations of small-cache repetition and claims about interpretability and generalization.

D1.justification: v2 adds layer-level KV-cache construction details, explicitly identifies Table 1 as using equal batch sizes, and mentions attempts with an LLM evaluator. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, and supplied prompts are retained. Concrete batch sizes and memory limits for the new timing study remain undocumented.

R1.justification: Appendix E.1 substantially repositions AnLLM: v1 calls it similar thought compression, whereas v2 emphasizes prompt compression and claims only a sparse-attention connection. Appendix E.4 and Table 5 add a structured comparison with implicit CoT, including newly cited System-1.5 and SoftThinking. LoRA and QLoRA references disappear with their limitation discussion.

P1.justification: The main discussion is redistributed into the overview and appendix, a mathematical appendix is inserted, and the discussion appendix gains numbered subsections. v2 also adds acknowledgments and makes localized wording and emphasis edits. Most of the original narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the equal-memory timing table and qualitative method-comparison table. It relocates and reformats the Dependency and AnLLM diagrams, adjusts some figure sizing and legends, and moves table placements. The retained efficiency, ablation, and compression-distribution plots preserve their numerical content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful equal-memory efficiency evidence and clearer compression mathematics; revised baseline scores also remove v1's CoT/Distill-R1 ranking inconsistency. However, the new timing study lacks concrete memory/batch settings, substantive limitations are dropped, and Appendix E.1's denial of similarity to AnLLM conflicts with Appendix C.2's retained description of a similar overall approach. These gains and losses leave the net quality change uncertain.
